History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe, "blinding" headache for 3 days, started suddenly on waking.
- Character/timing: Constant headache most of the time; pain severity reported as 8/10 at worst, decreasing to ~5/10 with analgesia.
- Location: Generalized, more severe over the right eye.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena described as "shooting light" / flashing lights; "feeling a bit sick" but no vomiting; some brief stabbing pain with sudden standing or rapid head movement.
- Relieving/aggravating factors: Partial temporary relief with ibuprofen; sleeps well and not awakened at night by the headache; sometimes worse on standing quickly or with head movement.
- Prior episodes: Occasional shorter headaches historically, most recently a 2-day headache responsive to ibuprofen; no prior prolonged headaches.
- Context: Missed one full workday and reduced work capacity while working from home during this 3-day period.
- Relevant negatives: No fever (patient did not feel feverish), no nausea with vomiting, no focal weakness, numbness, or tingling, no change in smell/taste, no sinus symptoms, no nosebleeds, no cough or hemoptysis.
- Recent care: Recent eye check reportedly normal (no change in vision noted by patient).
- Travel: No recent travel abroad.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Surgical history / hospitalizations: None reported.
- Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting.
- Allergies: Denies allergies.
- Medications:
  - Oral contraceptive ("the pill") — dose/route/frequency not documented (started ~1 year ago).
  - Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (used intermittently for headache).
  - No other regular medications reported.
- Social history: Lives alone; works from home; does not smoke; consumes alcohol (patient estimate: "three, once a week" — patient estimate; exact amount not documented). No recreational drug use reported.

Physical Examination:
- No physical or neurological examination performed during this remote consult.
- Reported clinical status: Patient able to communicate; not febrile by report.
- Relevant negatives reported by patient: No throat/ear/sinus pain, no visual acuity loss reported, no neurologic deficits reported.

Impression:
- Probable migraine-type headache per clinician assessment (visual aura/photophobia reported); further in-person evaluation required to exclude other causes.

Management Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face appointment for full examination including neurological exam, fundoscopy (examination of the back of the eyes), and blood pressure measurement.
- Prescribe a stronger analgesic to be taken instead of ibuprofen (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Paracetamol may be used concurrently with the prescribed analgesic (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Advice: Take the prescribed medication with food.
- Safety-netting: If headache worsens significantly, becomes unbearable, or changes character, go to A&E for urgent assessment. Contact clinician/support line for further advice as needed.
- Administrative: Book appointment via the support team; appointment may be canceled if symptoms resolve before the visit.
- Consideration: If migraines with aura are confirmed, clinician may advise changing the oral contraceptive; blood pressure will be checked to assess continued suitability of current pill.

Patient Summary:
- Patient developed a sudden, severe, constant headache 3 days ago with photophobia and intermittent flashing visual phenomena, partially responsive to ibuprofen. Clinician suspects a migraine-type headache but recommends an in-person neurological and eye examination and blood pressure check. A stronger analgesic has been prescribed for short-term symptom control; urgent care (A&E) advised if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Book and attend in-person appointment for neurological exam and fundoscopy; blood pressure will be checked.
- Start prescribed stronger analgesic (instead of ibuprofen) and paracetamol may be taken concurrently — take medications with food (specific medication details not documented).
- If headache becomes much worse, changes, or is unbearable, go to A&E or contact the clinician/support line.

Next Steps:
- Patient to arrange/support team booking for face-to-face appointment.
- At appointment: neurological examination, fundoscopy, and blood pressure measurement.
- Possible onward referral to headache/migraine specialist after in-person assessment if indicated; contraceptive review may be required depending on findings.
